title: Prayer, quiet, or ritual as your own tool
def: Many people find steadiness in prayer, silence, a familiar verse, or a small ritual; it is a personal practice, used in the person's own way or not at all.
look: what the person already finds comforting
a short quiet moment before acting
words or silence the person chooses
use: If you want, take a minute of quiet, prayer, or slow breathing, then return to the practical steps.
not: This is not medical treatment and does not replace calling for help.

title: Gratitude and meaning in hard times
def: Remembering what you are grateful for and who you are living for can strengthen the will to keep going through hardship.
look: thinking of family, friends, or faith
a reason to get through the night
use: Name three things you are grateful for, or the people waiting for you, and set one small goal for the next hour.
not: Do not force cheerfulness on someone who is grieving; follow their lead.

title: A moment of respect after a harvest
def: Many hunters pause after a kill to thank or honor the animal; it is a personal custom that often goes with using the meat well and wasting nothing.
look: a quiet moment with the animal
a plan to use the meat
use: Take a moment in your own way, then handle the animal with care and get the meat cool quickly.
not: Do not waste usable meat or leave the animal unrecovered without every effort.

title: Faith-community and support contacts on your card
def: A family card can hold contacts for the people who support you, such as a faith leader, a friend, or a counselor, along with crisis lines.
look: names and numbers written on paper as well as in the phone
a neighbor or friend who can check in
use: Add supporters to your family emergency card, ask them ahead of time whether you can call in a crisis, and keep a paper copy.
not: Do not rely on one phone for every number.
call: Call or text 988 any time for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; veterans can press 1. Call 911 if someone is in immediate danger.
